會試紀錄題辭

皇明設科，倣古者六藝之教，參以歷代遺制，欲兼收文武而用之。既詔天下三年一賓興，其薦于州郡者凡五百人，五抜其一而授之以官。猶以為未足，復勅有司自壬子至甲寅三歲連貢三百人，逮于乙卯始復初制，其恩至渥也。先是，京畿遵行鄉試，中式者七十二，未及貢南宫，上求治之切，皆采用之，至有為監察御史者。及是當會試之期，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

The August Ming established the civil service examinations in imitation of the ancient teaching of the Six Arts, consulting also the inherited institutions of successive dynasties, with the desire to recruit both civil and military talents and employ them. Having decreed that the realm should hold the triennial presentation of worthies, of the five hundred men recommended from the prefectures and counties in all, one out of five was to be selected and conferred an office. Still considering this insufficient, the Emperor further commanded the competent authorities that for three consecutive years, from the renzi year (1372) to the jiayin year (1374), three hundred men should be presented as tribute each year, and only when reaching the yimao year (1375) should the original system be restored; such imperial grace is most abundant indeed. Earlier, the Capital Region had complied in holding the Provincial Examination, and those who passed numbered seventy-two. Before they could be presented to the Southern Palace [Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination], His Majesty, in his earnest desire for good governance, selected and employed them all, to the point that some became Investigating Censors. Now, when the time for the Metropolitan Examination arrived, …

text:
若河南若陝西北平若山之
西東若江西湖廣若浙江若
廣之東西若福建其為行中
書十有一俊秀咸集而高句
麗之士與焉右丞相臣廣洋
左丞相臣惟庸同禮部尚書
臣凱臣訓文啓于
===

奏於是詔臣凱與前侍講學士

士臣同國子司業臣濂吏部
員外郎臣本前貢士臣恂與

title: 洪武四年會試錄
text:
凱等受命而出交相戒飭期
有以副
上旨遂議分經而考復互相叅定
使無所憾乃進于主司主司
徧觀而後次第之猶慮滄海
有遺珠之嘆卷之已黜者復
覆視而致謹焉晝盡其力夜
向午燭影熒熒於簾几間不
敢自寧士之就試者一百八
十九在選者踰百人署名于
榜用鼓吹導至中書掲而張
之内司卷官吏部侍郎臣貞

translation_en: …Kai 凱 and the others received the command and withdrew, mutually admonishing one another in the hope of fulfilling His Majesty's intent. We thereupon agreed to divide the examination papers by Classic to assess them, and then cross-checked and decided upon them together so that there would be no cause for regret, before submitting them to the Chief Examiners. After the Chief Examiners had read through them all and ranked them in order, still fearing the lament of leaving pearls behind in the vast sea, they re-examined the papers that had already been rejected and exercised the utmost care over them. By day we exhausted our strength, and as night approached midnight, with candle shadows flickering between the screens and tables, we did not dare take our ease. Of the one hundred and eighty-nine scholars who sat for the examination, more than a hundred were selected. Their names were inscribed on the placard, which was escorted with drums and pipes to the Secretariat and posted on display. title: 洪武四年會試錄
text:
編簡以傳書有之野無遺賢
萬邦咸寧夫賢之在野無以
自見多由進士而升名于天
府故昔人謂進士為將相科
姑以宋言之深沉有德如王
旦面折廷争如寇準出當方
面如張詠盖不可以勝數至
===
今科目倚之以為重與茲選
掄者當思以前脩自勗以忠
貞佐
國家而致黎民於變時雍之治
庶於明體適用之學或無所
愧不然則是錄之行他日將
有指其名而議之者矣可不

punctuated: 編簡以傳。《書》有之：「野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。」夫賢之在野，無以自見，多由進士而升名于天府，故昔人謂進士為將相科。姑以宋言之，深沉有德如王旦，面折廷争如寇準，出當方面如張詠，盖不可以勝數，至今科目倚之以為重。與茲選掄者，當思以前脩自勗，以忠貞佐國家，而致黎民於變時雍之治，庶於明體適用之學，或無所愧。不然，則是錄之行，他日將有指其名而議之者矣，可不
translation_en: … into a volume to be handed down. It is said in the Book of Documents (Shu): "When no men of worth are left neglected in the countryside, all the myriad states enjoy peace." Indeed, when men of worth are in the countryside and have no means of making themselves known, it is mostly through the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) that their names are raised to the imperial repository. For this reason, people of former times called the metropolitan graduate degree the "examination for generals and chief councilors." To speak provisionally of the Song dynasty: men of deep composure and virtue such as Wang Dan 王旦, men who rebuked the ruler to his face and contended in court such as Kou Zhun 寇準, and men who went out to take charge of regional commands such as Zhang Yong 張詠 were truly too numerous to count; down to the present day, the examination system relies on them for its prestige. Those who participate in this selection ought to reflect on exhorting themselves after the example of those former worthies, assisting the State with loyalty and integrity, and bringing about a governance in which the black-haired people are transformed and live in harmony; thus, perhaps, they will have nothing to be ashamed of with respect to learning that illuminates fundamental principles and meets practical needs. Otherwise, when this record is circulated, in days to come there will be those who point to their names and criticize them. How can they not…
